chunks: I asked al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): 'When may I strike my animal under me?' He said: 'When it does not walk under you as it walks to its feeding place.'

key_terms.مذود: Feeding place, manger — where the animal eats; used as a measure of the animal's natural motivation

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to strike a riding animal according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: A narrator reports asking Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the permissibility of striking one's riding animal. The Imam gave a practical criterion: one may strike the animal only when it is not walking at its natural, motivated pace — specifically, not moving as eagerly as when it heads toward its own food. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle of kindness and responsibility toward animals, framing permitted correction only when the animal is actually being sluggish.
